title: Strict-Transport-Security max-age is not a valid delta-seconds value
description: The HSTS header carries a max-age directive whose value is not an unsigned decimal integer: it is empty, negative, fractional, or contains trailing characters. A user agent that cannot parse delta-seconds discards the whole header, so the site has no HSTS policy at all while its operators believe one is deployed. Quoted values are excluded here because DPK-DAST-024 already reports every quoted max-age as invalid.
remediation: Send max-age as a bare unsigned integer number of seconds, for example max-age=31536000. Validate the value at the framework or proxy layer so a template error cannot ship a non-numeric duration.
limitation: One header value. The rule judges the max-age syntax visible in the response; it cannot prove that a browser discarded the header, and quoted values are graded by DPK-DAST-024 instead.
scopeT: One response whose Strict-Transport-Security max-age directive is present with an unquoted, non-numeric or missing value.
fp: A deployment that deliberately sends a non-numeric placeholder during a rollout is reported; the browser ignores the header in that state either way.
recordDesc: Strict-Transport-Security carries a max-age directive that is not a plain unsigned integer. Parsers reject the directive, and HSTS processing stops for the whole header, so the origin loses the protection the header was meant to establish: the next plaintext navigation is not upgraded and the browser records no HSTS state.
risk: No HSTS enforcement despite an HSTS header being present; MEDIUM severity, matching a missing policy.
why: The max-age directive has no value, or its value is not digits followed by a directive boundary.
fix: Emit max-age=<unsigned seconds> with no quotes and no units.
Add a response-header test that rejects non-numeric max-age values.
verifyT: Request the endpoint over HTTPS and confirm max-age is an unsigned integer that a strict parser accepts.
